chunks: He said: And Abu Abdillah Lizaz narrated to me from Sarim bin Alwan al-Jawkhi, who said: I, along with Mufaddal, Yunus bin Zabyan, al-Fayd bin al-Mukhtar, and Qasim (partner of Mufaddal), entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and his son Ismail was with him.

Al-Fayd said: May I be your ransom, we accept the estates/lands from these people, and we accept them paying more than what we take from them. He said: There is no harm in it. His son Ismail said to him: You did not understand, O Father! Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I did not understand? I told you to stay with me (be patient/attentive), but you do not listen. Ismail rose in anger. Al-Fayd said: We think that he is the master of this affair (the Imam) after you. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: No, by Allah, he is not so. Then he said: This one is more fitting for me than that, and he pointed to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was sleeping, and embraced him so he slept on his chest. When he awoke, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) took his arm and said: This, by Allah, is my son truly; he, by Allah, will fill it with justice and equity, just as it was filled with injustice and tyranny. Qasim said to him a second time: This one, may I be your ransom? He said: Yes, by Allah, this is my son; he will not leave the world until Allah fills the earth with him with justice and equity, just as it was filled with injustice and tyranny. He swore three oaths.
ai.seo_question: Who is the designated successor of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the pivotal moment of succession (Nass) from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq to Imam Musa al-Kadhim, explicitly refuting the Waqifiyya who held that Ismail predeceased him and thus blocked his path to the Imamate. The Imam’s three oaths and the physical gesture of embracing the sleeping Abu al-Hasan underscore the divine certainty of the designation, linking the current Imamate to the eschatological promise of the Mahdi. This narrative serves as a foundational proof for the continuity of the Imamate through the sons of the Imams, a core tenet of Twelver Shia theology.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 37 - Narrated to me Abu Abdullah Lizaz from Sarim bin Alwan Jokhi: I, Mufaddal, Yunus bin Zabyan, Faiz bin Mukhtar, Qasim, partner of Mufaddal came to meet Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s); and his son, Ismail, was also present there.

Faiz asked: May I be your ransom, what if we accept monies, which people are having [which they cannot use or spend in any lawful manner] and guarantee to pay more than what we take. His Eminence said: There is no problem in it. Ismail said to the Imam: Father dear, you didn’t pay attention to the problem. The Imam said: I did not understand? (many times); I told you to be with me, so that I may understand these problems, but you don’t listen to me. Ismail arose in fury and went away. Faiz said: We thought that he is the Imam after you. Imam (a.s) said: No, by Allah, it is not so. Then he said: This is the one who is my assistant and deputy in Imamate and he pointed to Abul Hasan, Musa (a.s), who was asleep. Imam (a.s) took him in his arms and made him sleep on his chest. When he awoke, Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) took his hand and said: By God, indeed this son of mine (is the Imam after me). By God, he would fill the earth with justice and equity, just as it would be fraught with injustice and tyranny. Qasim, partner of Mufaddal said: May I be your ransom, this boy? Imam (a.s) replied: Yes, by God, he is the one; and he would not leave the world till through him the Almighty Allah fills up the earth with justice and equity, just as it would have been fraught with oppression and tyranny, and the Imam swore thrice.
